name: Should I choose a double vanity or a single vanity with more counter space?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a double vanity or a single vanity with more counter space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Double vanities provide dedicated storage and separate prep stations for couples, but they require a minimum width of 60 inches to avoid feeling cramped and sacrifice valuable floor space. A single vanity preserves open floor space, leaves room for a larger walk-in shower or linen cabinet, and costs less in materials, mirrors, and plumbing rough-ins. When planning a shared master bathroom, decide whether you value simultaneous sink access more than open floor clearance or expanded shower dimensions. Measure the door swing and entryway clearance carefully before selecting a wide vanity cabinet.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a double vanity if you have at least 60 inches of wall width and need simultaneous sink access; otherwise, a single vanity allows for a larger shower and more open room.
